heading: How return values become responses
body:
An ordinary return value becomes JSON. A response in the language's own type controls status, headers and body, such as a Fetch `Response` in JavaScript, `http::Response` in Rust, `HttpResponseMessage` in C# or an `(HTTPStatus, headers, body)` tuple in Python. Java, Groovy and Kotlin write the answer on the `HttpExchange` argument, PHP uses `http_response_code()`, `header()` and `echo`, and Ruby and Lua return a `[status, headers, body]` list. Yon sends HTML only when the controller method itself selects `Content-Type: text/html`. Yon passes those bytes through unchanged. It does no interpolation (filling values into text), no component expansion, no control-tag evaluation and no server-side rendering. Tachyon rejects a `yon.html` file with TY1008.

C++ has no tab here, because a C++ route method cannot return a native response yet: it returns a value, which Tachyon writes as JSON with status 200, or 204 for `void` (ADR 0099).
